notToBeConfusedWith.name: Mezcal
notToBeConfusedWith.note: Tequila is one specific style of mezcal, made only from blue agave in a defined region and almost always in column stills; mezcal is the wider category and is usually pot-distilled with a smokier roast.

generalSubstitutes.note: Both are agave spirits, but mezcal's smoke is a flavour the recipe may not want; using it whole in place of tequila changes the drink rather than merely standing in for it.

forms.label: Blanco
forms.sourceNote: Tequila, a generic survey record rather than a specific brand. Public domain. 40% alc./vol. is the standard bottling strength for tequila under Mexican regulation. Unaged and bottled shortly after distillation, so its own macros are the record's straight figures with no barrel-derived sugar to add. No measured liquid density exists for tequila at this dataset; the density-classes.json 'spirit-40' class is used and marked estimated.
